Maria: Heads-up — nightly perf alert flagged a 12% p50 regression on the nvlink pool for the chat-small model compared to yesterday. CI diff: https://dash.redwood/perf/1765 :eyes:
perf-ci-bot: nightly-run 1765 completed. Summary: 1 regression, 3 improvements, 2 flaky tests. Regression: chat-small @ nvlink (p50 +12%).
Ajay: Ugh. Did the alert include which kernel variant was used?
Maria: It did — kernel v3.4.1 was selected by the policy. Yesterday's golden was v3.3.7. Also saw increased KV miss rate in the profile.
Taylor: Can you paste the perf profile snippet?
Maria: Sure — from the replay harness for the failing trace:
```
KV cache hit_rate: 0.64 -> 0.48
Batch size distribution: median 4 -> 6
Kernel chosen: aten_gemm_v2 (v3.4.1)
Timeline: stall spikes at 90-120ms token window
```
Chris: That lower KV hit rate stands out. If batching increased median to 6, cache alignment could differ and cause more recompute. Could be a change in prefix hashing in the runtime or replay harness ordering skew.
Zoe: I also noticed a small change in the kernel selector heuristics that prefers aten_gemm_v2 for seq_len <= 256 when throughput predicted higher. Deployed in v3.4.x.
Ajay: So hypothesis A: kernel selector change + different batch shape => worse end-to-end latency for this workload. Hypothesis B: KV cache eviction/lookup semantics changed, leading to more misses.
Maria: Repro steps I used in the replay harness: same seed, same request trace (prod-trace-20260316), 10k requests, concurrency=32. We should reproduce apples-to-apples: force kernel v3.3.7 and v3.4.1 with identical batching heuristics and KV policy.
perf-ci-bot: note: created perf-1765-issue linked to internal tracker: PERF-1765.
Taylor: I'll run a differential replay comparing kernel variants with explicit KV policy flags. Running job now (repro/1765/compare).
Chris: Add a run that pins batch sizing to yesterday's observed distribution: --batch-policy=static --batch-median=4. Also include a run with prefix-only KV caching to isolate lookup behavior.
Taylor: Good call. Also will snapshot CPU/GPU timelines and kernel counters. If we see kernel-level time increase but same kv miss rate, it points to kernel regression.
Zoe: If it is selector heuristics, we should tweak selector cost model rather than reverting kernel. Possibly bump penalty for aten_gemm_v2 on nvlink for these shapes.
Ajay: For CI: we should avoid flaky alerts. Proposal: require regression to show up in both synthetic replay and production-trace replays, and run 3 repeats before firing alert. Also add a delta-stability check to reduce noise.
Maria: Sounds good. Action items:
- Taylor: run differential replays (kernel pinned, batch pinned, kv policy pinned) and attach traces to PERF-1765.
- Ajay: update CI alerting to 3-run confirmation and add reproducibility requirement.
- Zoe: audit selector change PR (merge: runtime#4821) for cost-model assumptions.
- Chris: add a short-lived per-test flag to mark flaky nightly tests to suppress pager until triaged.
Taylor: Started the runs, ETA ~30m. I'll post concise results here and link dashboards.
perf-ci-bot: run repro/1765/compare: queued -> running (job id: r-1765-9). Logs: https://ci.redwood/repro/1765/9/logs
Maria: Thanks team. Once we have the diff, we can decide whether to rollback kernel selector tweak or adjust batching defaults. If KV semantics are the culprit, fix fast in runtime and add unit test for prefix hash stability. :thumbsup:
Taylor: Quick interim note: first run (pin v3.3.7) p50=82ms, second run (pin v3.4.1) p50=92ms, KV hit_rate 0.66 vs 0.49. Looks like KV behavior is primary. Dumping full profile to PERF-1765.
Chris: If KV hit rate drops that much just by kernel/selector change, there's probably an ordering or hashing side-effect. I'll grep the PR for any key-serialization touches.
Zoe: I'll prepare a hotfix that makes selector opt-in until we confirm. We can add an A/B rollout in dedicated to validate.
Maria: Excellent. Keep updates in-thread. We'll aim to suppress noisy alerts until triage complete.
Taylor: Uploaded full traces + flamegraphs to PERF-1765. Will annotate suspected segments.
Ajay: After triage, we should add a CI regression test reproducer that runs on every kernel selector change: small replay + kv smoke + apples-to-apples compare. That should catch regressions earlier.
Maria: Agreed. Closing loop: I'll update the nightly alert doc with the 3-run confirmation policy and link to this thread. Thanks all.
perf-ci-bot: nightly-run 1765 follow-ups: issue PERF-1765 created, triage tag added, flaky-test suppression applied to test_id: nightly-replay-14.
